headline: Ten Things on the Big 5 Floor That Solve a Problem a Contractor Has Today
deck: Not the demonstrations that draw a crowd. The products with a part number, a certificate and somebody in the Kingdom who can service them.
excerpt: A walk through Big 5 Construct Saudi filtered for one test: does this solve a problem a Saudi contractor has on a live job this month. Ten exhibits pass, from low-GWP refrigerants and carbon-declared valves to ground improvement, locally formulated admixtures and integrated facilities management.
content:
Every large construction show has two floors running at once. One is the future: the demonstration that draws a crowd, the robot that lays a metre of brickwork while a camera watches, the platform that promises to unify data nobody has collected yet. The other is the floor where a project engineer with a problem this month finds something with a part number, a test certificate and a technician in the Kingdom. Walking Big 5 Construct Saudi against that second test, ten exhibits stood out.

The first is refrigerant chemistry. Prime Middle East Trading Company, trading as PRIMECO, took the show's Sustainability Innovation award for the Solstice low global warming potential range, and the reason it belongs on a practical list is that the substitution happens inside equipment that is being bought anyway. R-1234ze goes into air-cooled and water-cooled chillers and heat pumps; R-1234yf sits close to a drop-in for R-134a. The decision is made once and lives in the plant room for two decades.

The second is carbon transparency on a commodity item. Galaxy Technology is showing Albion Valves with declared carbon figures across its cast-iron range. A valve is not an interesting product. A valve with a number a specifier can put in a submittal, when the client has an embodied-carbon target and no data to meet it with, is a genuinely useful one.

Third, wood-based panels. Masdar's Kronospan boards took Best Circular Economy Solution on the show's sustainability trail, recognised on a carbon-negative basis. Fit-out, joinery and furniture packages buy panels by the container, and this is one of the few places where a materials swap does not require a design change.

Fourth, roofing that also insulates. Star Factory's spray polyurethane foam roofing and waterproofing answers two line items with one application, which matters on the flat roofs of warehouses and industrial sheds where the cooling load is set by the roof and the leak risk is set by the joints.

Fifth, ground improvement. Keller was on the trail with foundation and ground improvement work, and it is the least fashionable and most valuable item on this list. Programme is lost under the slab far more often than above it, and treating weak ground rather than excavating it removes haulage, imported fill and traffic movements from the critical path.

Sixth, integrated facilities management with energy management attached. Al-Futtaim Engineering Company took the Operational Sustainability award for exactly that combination. Saudi Arabia has commissioned an enormous quantity of asset in a short period, and the operating cost of that estate is now a larger number than the construction cost of the next tranche.

Seventh, fire and life safety as a single portfolio. NAFFCO is showing fire safety, life safety and security technologies together, which reflects how these packages are now tendered on complex developments — as one interfaced system rather than three subcontracts that meet for the first time during commissioning.

Eighth, structural steel with a domestic supply story. Al Yamamah Steel Industries is showing structural steel for infrastructure and buildings. In a market where lead time is frequently the binding constraint, a fabricator inside the Kingdom is a schedule instrument as much as a materials supplier.

Ninth, construction chemicals formulated locally. Arkaz, exhibiting here for the first time, designs and produces concrete admixture systems and specialty building materials through plants in Dammam and Jeddah. Admixtures are where a ready-mix producer buys workability, set time and durability, and where they are formulated determines how quickly a mix can be adjusted when site conditions move.

Tenth, integrated building solutions sold as one package. CPC Holding is showing construction and building solutions as a combined offer, which is less a technology than a procurement answer to the interface risk that consumes main contractors on multi-package jobs.

What connects the ten is not novelty. It is that each one attaches to a purchase order somebody is already raising, and each one can be checked. That is a low bar in principle and a surprisingly high one in practice, and it is the bar the buyers walking these halls are applying.
author: Mo Qureshi
